# Limits, open questions, and directions {#sec-limits}

**Every claim in this book has a boundary, and this chapter states each one
as a fact about the evidence: what was measured, on which split, with which
instrument, and what would move it.** The claims themselves live in the
evidence chapters with their numbers; here each is reduced to its limit, so
that a reader can tell a settled result from an open one at a glance, and
the chapter ends with the two outcomes that would change the
recommendation.

```{python}
#| label: setup-limits
#| include: false
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
RES = Path("..") / "results"
mean = statistics.mean
```

## What is established {#sec-established}

Eight results are settled to the standard of the fair-comparison protocol
(@sec-protocol). Each carries its numbers and its scope in its home
section; this chapter adds only the limits.

| result | where |
|---|---|
| On HiLiftAeroML surface pressure, GeoTransolver and Transolver fed the unit freestream direction lead ISLA at every rung where it is measured: 35 and 210 random training cases, 4 and 21 training geometries, and the fixed angle; on the 35-case rung the deficit is not count noise (0.73 at the reporting protocol of 200,000 cells against 0.72 at the exploration budget). | @sec-data-efficiency, @sec-scoreboard-200k |
| On DrivAerML at the reporting protocol ISLA and GeoTransolver are at parity at full data (0.998) and ISLA leads Transolver by 6%; below full data GeoTransolver is the more data-efficient model, by a deficit that narrows from 17% at 27 cars to zero at 435. At the exploration budget the baselines led by a few percent; that gap's anatomy is known and the denser budget closed it. | @sec-scoreboard-200k, @sec-full-data, @sec-deficit-anatomy |
| Rotation and translation covariance are exact by construction; with every case in a random pose ISLA scores 1.015x its native-frame error and leads the augmented baselines by 12% and 21% at the reporting protocol (7% and 17% at the exploration budget; @sec-nb-p200k-pose-verdict, @sec-nb-poseref-verdict). | @sec-pose, @sec-mt2-contracts |
| The relative frame is consistent under a change of surface sampling where every sample-centered configuration collapses, and the measure-weighted ISLA arms are the only ones that converge under refinement. | @sec-consistency-bench, @sec-scoreboard-consistency |
| Training needs no rate sweep at the protocol rate 1e-3, but the safe window is narrower than the baselines' (at width 192, 3e-3 collapses and 1e-2 diverges; @sec-nb-lrref-verdict); the step cost is at parity with GeoTransolver at 10,000 tokens in half the memory. | @sec-robustness-lr, @sec-mt2-cost |
| On the interior task ISLA leads GeoTransolver-volume on velocity at a third of the parameters, trails on pressure and eddy viscosity, and leads on two of three fields at matched parameters. | @sec-interior |
| Nothing tested generalizes across a flow-regime boundary. | @sec-regime-extrapolation |
| Cross-family transfer is a property of the training data for every architecture tested. | @sec-limits-transfer |

## Limits of each headline claim {#sec-review-honesty}

### The HiLiftAeroML ladder: what its curves measure {#sec-limits-data-efficiency}

**The unit-direction baselines lie below ISLA at
both rungs where it is measured, at a ratio that narrows from the smaller
training set to the larger; the ladder is a statement about the range of
data every production CFD dataset in this program occupies, not a scaling
law.** The
quantity throughout is the surface-pressure relative L2 of @sec-metrics
averaged over the 180 validation cases shared by every rung, in float32.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ladder-unit-drive
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The HiLiftAeroML ladder under the unit-direction protocol. Surface
#|   pressure error on the shared 180-case validation set against the number
#|   of training cases, log-log, float32; marks are seed means and small dots
#|   the individual seeds. ISLA (filled blue
#|   squares), GeoTransolver (red circles) and Transolver (amber triangles,
#|   dashed) at the two rungs where the reference is trained, 35 and 210
#|   cases, each at its declared learning rate. How to read this: the
#|   baselines lie below the reference at both rungs; ISLA
#|    is not measured at 510 or 1,260 cases, so those rungs are
#|   not shown and its ratio there is not known. It does not show the
#|   geometry and fixed-angle splits (@sec-scoreboard). Protocol: 10,000
#|   sampled cells per case, 500 epochs, bfloat16 training, no augmentation.
#|   Data: results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_2026-09-09.json,
#|   results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_35_2026-09-09.json,
#|   results/udrvl_210_reduction_2026-09-10.json,
#|   results/relframe_reduction_2026-09-11.json,
#|   results/frame_reduction_2026-09-11.json.
#| code-fold: true
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
fpall = J("fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_2026-09-09.json")["runs"]; fp35 = J("fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_35_2026-09-09.json")["runs"]
u210 = J("udrvl_210_reduction_2026-09-10.json")
rf = J("relframe_reduction_2026-09-11.json")["hilift_val"]; ff = J("frame_reduction_2026-09-11.json")["hilift_val"]
p32 = lambda runs, names: [runs[n]["fields"]["pressure_l2"]["fp32_mean"] for n in names]
a210 = u210["three_seed_addendum_fp32"]
series = {
    "isla_ref": {35: [rf[f"rf_hl_mt2_meas_super_scarce_seed{s}"]["pressure_l2"] for s in (42, 43)],
                 210: [ff[f"rf_hl_mt2_meas_scarce_seed{s}"]["pressure_l2"] for s in (42, 43)]},
    "gt": {35: p32(fp35, [f"udrv_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3_seed{s}" for s in (42, 43)]),
           210: a210["gt_unit_lr1e3"]["seed_pressure"]},
    "t": {35: p32(fp35, [f"udrv_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3_seed{s}" for s in (42, 43, 44)]),
          210: a210["transolver_unit_lr3e3"]["seed_pressure"]},
}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.9))
for key in ("isla_ref", "gt", "t"):
    d = series[key]; xs = sorted(d)
    ax.plot(xs, [mean(d[x]) for x in xs], **series_kwargs(key, zorder=3))
    for x in xs:
        ax.scatter([x] * len(d[x]), d[x], s=12, color=STYLE[key]["color"], zorder=4)
lines = ["baseline ÷ ISLA (seed means)"]
for x in (35, 210):
    ref = mean(series["isla_ref"][x])
    lines.append(f"{x:,} cases: GeoTransolver {mean(series['gt'][x])/ref:.2f}, Transolver {mean(series['t'][x])/ref:.2f}")
lines.append("510 and 1,260 cases: reference not yet measured")
note(ax, "\n".join(lines), loc="lower left")
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xticks([35, 210, 510, 1260]); ax.set_xticklabels(["35", "210", "510", "1,260"])
ax.set_yticks([0.04, 0.06, 0.1, 0.15]); ax.set_yticklabels(["0.04", "0.06", "0.10", "0.15"])
ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax.set_xlim(25, 1800); ax.set_ylim(0.035, 0.2)
ax.set_xlabel("training cases [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface pressure error, area-weighted relative L2 [–]")
ax.set_title("HiLiftAeroML nested splits, unit-direction protocol, float32")
ax.grid(True, which="major"); ax.grid(False, which="minor")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Three facts bound what the curves can say.

- **ISLA is measured at two rungs.** At 510 and
  1,260 cases it is not yet trained, so its ratio on the two largest rungs
  is not known; the baselines' curves continue to those rungs
  (@sec-scoreboard), and the expectation from the recurrence reading below
  is a ratio somewhat lower than at 210 cases.
- **Every seed at a rung trains on the same curated subset**, so the seed
  bands measure initialization, not the choice of training cases.
  Geometry-stratified redraws of the 35- and 210-case training sets put the
  GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA ratio inside a band that stays below one on every
  draw (@sec-scoreboard), so the curated draws are typical.
- **The flattening toward 1,260 cases is not a token floor.** Retrained at
  20,000 cells per case, GeoTransolver and ISLA (the legacy centered variant,
  used here as a diagnostic) improve by about the same factor and their
  ratio does not move (@sec-scoreboard-protocol); the two architectures
  share most of their residual on identical points at that rung
  (@sec-shared-floor), so the floor is the labels' or the protocol's, not
  one architecture's.

### The HiLift accuracy figures are validation-set figures {#sec-limits-validation}

**Every HiLiftAeroML accuracy number in this book is scored on the shared
180-case validation set on final-epoch checkpoints; no checkpoint is
selected on validation error, but no HiLiftAeroML split remains that could
confirm the numbers independently of the program's own history.** The
validation set entered more than one decision: each architecture's
learning-rate choice on the full split (@sec-lr-protocol), Transolver's
rate per small-data rung, the design of the ablations, and the choice of
what to present. The sealed test splits were spent on regime extrapolation
and the deflection split, which train on different cases but between them
read every one of the 180 geometries, and their manifests overlap the
data-efficiency test set on most of its cases
(results/hilift_exposure_ledger_2026-09-08.json). Every remaining test
split is therefore *held out per checkpoint*, since no model trained on
it, but not a *program-level confirmation*, and removing already-read cases
after the fact would define a selected population, not a replacement. A
sealed evaluation of the 35-case checkpoints on the 360 test cases would be
a within-protocol held-out check of the 35-case ratios and is not yet
measured (@sec-program-status); an independent confirmation needs
geometries no part of the program has scored, which on HiLiftAeroML means a
prospective dataset.

### Mechanism: what is known and what is not {#sec-limits-mechanism}

**The in-distribution gap is decomposed, and the parts that remain
unexplained are small; what is not known is whether any of them can be
removed without breaking a contract.** The decomposition itself is
@sec-deficit-anatomy; the limits on it are these.

- **No single ingredient of ISLA is load-bearing for its own accuracy.**
  Five single-factor ablations at 35 wing cases each move the error by
  between −12% and +16% (@sec-mechanism). The exactness of the covariance
  contract neither costs nor buys anything measurable in distribution at
  that rung; at 435 cars the positional information the contracts deny is
  worth about two and a half points of the ratio, measured by a diagnostic
  that breaks the contract and is not a configuration
  (@sec-deficit-anatomy).
- **The surface deficit is representational, not a shortage of training
  cases.** With the data axis removed (one case, 64 resampled views, trained
  to convergence: the error reached this way is the model's *one-car
  floor*, a measurement of capacity rather than of generalization), ISLA's
  floor is above both baselines' by more than the
  35-case gap on both datasets; the deficit sits on the smooth, large-cell
  regions that dominate the area-weighted metric, not at the gaps between
  wing elements (@sec-nb-overfit-verdict). Which part of the representation
  carries it is partly known: on the one-car instrument, eight independent
  routings per block remove most of it, and whether that transfers to the
  full training set is the open run (@sec-program-status).
- **The relative frame's price on the wings is mesher pattern.** Against
  the legacy centered variant (a diagnostic here: a plain-mean center with a
  fixed length unit) the reference pays nothing on DrivAerML and on the
  never-seen-geometry rungs, and about a tenth where validation geometries
  recur in training. Two diagnostics with an exact full-geometry frame pay
  more than the reference, so the price is not positional information but
  the mesh-density content of the plain-mean center, which is reusable when
  a wing returns and a liability when it does not
  (@sec-nb-frame-full-verdict). The fixed angle is the one
  never-seen-geometry rung where the reference still pays; the reading that
  a single freestream direction makes the mesher's refinement pattern a
  geometric cue that transfers within the wing family is consistent with
  every rung and not separately tested.
- **The measure weights' price is variance plus mesh pattern, and only the
  variance part shrinks.** On the cars the weights-off ÷ weights-on ratio
  rises toward one with cell count; on the wings it is flat across a
  sixteen-fold range, which variance cannot produce, and the weights-off
  checkpoints collapse under an area-proportional draw to errors worse than
  predicting zero (@sec-consistency-bench). Weights off is an ablation that
  prices the measure semantics, never a configuration (@sec-principle).
- **The interior standings sort into capacity and generalization** on the
  single-car instrument: the velocity lead is capacity, the eddy-viscosity
  deficit is capacity too and more cars will not close it, and the pressure
  standing reverses with the data fixed, so what pressure lead ISLA has at
  full data is generalization across cars (@sec-interior-open).
- **The contracts are exact in float32 and not in bf16.** On the trained
  GPU path the rotation and translation residual is 3e-5 at worst in
  float32 and 4% (pressure) to 7% (wall shear) under the bf16 autocast the
  recipe trains with, mostly ordinary rounding (2.3% with no motion at all).
  A bf16 deployment does not exercise the contracts at the level the book
  claims for them; float32 inference does (@sec-mt2-contracts,
  @sec-using-sampler).

### Regime extrapolation fails for every architecture tested {#sec-limits-regime}

**Neither architecture generalizes across a flow-regime boundary, and
ISLA's structure does not change that.** The readout is the out-of-regime
sealed-test pressure error divided by the in-regime validation error.
Trained at angles of attack up to 12° and tested at 14° and above, or
trained pre-stall and tested post-stall, both architectures lose about a
factor of ten, and the out-of-regime errors are worse than either reaches
from 35 in-regime cases (@sec-regime-extrapolation). Both GeoTransolver
regime runs consumed the physical velocity, so the ratios there are
physical-velocity measurements; ISLA keeps the lower absolute error on both
sides of the boundary. Whether GeoTransolver's smaller degradation ratio
comes from its raw-coordinate inputs was tested directly with a
raw-coordinate channel on ISLA (which breaks the covariance contract); the
preregistered falsifier fired, so the smaller ratio is not carried by raw
coordinates and no mechanism for it has been isolated
(@sec-ood-mechanism). Coverage of the regime, not architecture, governs
this axis. Along one geometry parameter of one wing family the picture is
the same: on the deflection split, trained on the milder 80% of geometries
and tested once on the most aggressive 20%, both architectures degrade by
the same factor and the in-regime ordering carries through
(@sec-nb-deflection-verdict). A split across geometry *classes* remains the
open test, and none of this book's datasets provides one.

### Interior accuracy {#sec-limits-interior}

**The interior standing, a velocity lead and a pressure and eddy-viscosity
deficit at a third of the parameters, holds at the training query count on
one dataset, and its eddy-viscosity part is a capacity limit located in the
far wake.** Four limits bound it (@sec-interior). The comparison is not
resource-matched and the two models do not receive the same inputs, and
GeoTransolver-volume fed the physical velocity changes by under 2% on every
field, so the ratios are not an input-scale artifact. The full-data
standings only partly extend to small data: at 54 and 109 training cars
the velocity lead is smaller and the eddy-viscosity deficit unchanged
(@tbl-interior-smalldata). The interacting decode's prediction depends on
the joint query set, training over a range of counts reduces the
dependence without removing it, and the passive decode's dependence is
exactly zero, so the interacting configuration is deployed at its training
count (@sec-interior-companion). And the eddy-viscosity metric is on a
standardized field, so its ratios are orderings under that centering, not
physical percentages. The open item is the far-wake eddy-viscosity gap:
anchor geometry, training-time sampling and query-side inputs do not close
it, width narrows it without closing it, and the single-car test identifies
it as capacity (@sec-interior-open).

### Exact query independence costs about three times in accuracy {#sec-limits-query-independence}

**ISLA's surface predictions depend weakly on which other points are
sampled; making them exactly independent costs 3.0 to 3.7x in surface
accuracy, so every surface checkpoint behind the headline results is the
interacting configuration** (@sec-query-independence). Swapping the
companion set moves a surface point's prediction by about 7%
(GeoTransolver's by about 2% at a shared prefix). The passive decoder is
exactly independent in float64 and 3.0 to 3.7x less accurate on DrivAerML
surface pressure, and the interior confirms the price at matched depth and
inputs: a twelve-block passive decode from an interacting support set
carrying the signed distance still costs 1.43x on pressure and 2.41x on
eddy viscosity against the interacting query tokens
(@sec-interior-query-independence). What the interacting queries provide is
computation at the requested points through every encoder layer, not
geometric context. Evaluate-anywhere semantics is a contract with a measured
price, and ISLA does not carry it.

### Cross-family transfer is a data property {#sec-limits-transfer}

**Neither ISLA nor GeoTransolver transfers zero-shot across vehicle
families; what moves cross-family error is the diversity of the training
data, and ISLA pays more than GeoTransolver for both halving its source
data and mixing in a sibling family** (@tbl-frontier in @sec-full-data).
On the held-out fastback family the models trained on DrivAerML alone score
close to the mean predictor, ISLA's failure worse than GeoTransolver's, and
a second training family moves both to a usable error. Few-shot adaptation
separates them further: fine-tuned on 20 fastback cases, GeoTransolver's
head start over training from scratch grows while ISLA's shrinks, so what
GeoTransolver learns on DrivAerML is the better starting point for a new
family (research/transfer_program/studies/campaign_c_transfer). No single
ISLA ingredient carries that deficit: retraining with more or fewer
anchors, raw seeds, the similarity-gauge variant (diagnostic) or the weights off moves the
zero-shot error nowhere near GeoTransolver's (@sec-nb-xfam-verdict), so the
cross-family question is a data question. Diversity at a fixed label budget
is a trade: splitting 435 training cases between DrivAerML and a sibling
family buys the target family almost entirely and costs the source about
what halving its data costs, plus a few percent for the mixing, and the
mixing cost grows with the foreign share for ISLA and not for GeoTransolver;
a per-case family flag changes nothing, so the mismatch is coverage, not
identification. A claim of family-portable surface physics from any of
these architectures would need a corpus in which geometry, pose, scale and
regime vary one at a time.

## Open questions, and what would settle each {#sec-open-questions}

Each open question carries a preregistered readout and bar before it runs;
the live status of every item is in @sec-program-status, and the
preregistrations are in the notebook. Unless stated, the readout is the
surface-pressure relative L2 of @sec-metrics and the ratio is baseline ÷
ISLA, so above one favors ISLA.

| question | what would settle it | bar |
|---|---|---|
| What is the mechanism of the wing deficit? | the mesher-pattern hypothesis (validation geometries recur in training with a different mesh) tested by a split that holds geometries out entirely at matched case count, at the reporting protocol | the ratio moves toward parity when recurrence is removed, or does not |
| Does the routing-multiplicity gain measured on one car transfer to the full DrivAerML training set? | ISLA with 4 and 8 routings per block at 435 cars, two seeds, on the sample-frame probe (10,000 cells, uniform and 10:1-biased draws) | closes the form gap at or below the value the anatomy assigns to a model without the form deficit; carries at a 2% gain; null under 1% (@sec-nb-heads435-prereg) |
| What is ISLA's ratio on the two largest HiLift rungs? | the reference trained at 510 and 1,260 cases under the frozen protocol | reported as measured; the prediction from the recurrence reading is a ratio somewhat below the 210-case value |
| Do the 35-case ratios hold on cases no decision has read? | the 35-case ISLA and unit-direction baseline checkpoints scored once on the 360-case sealed test | the validation ratios reproduced within their seed spread |
| Is the width learning-rate rule a scaling law or a one-corner fix? | a width ladder at fixed cells with the rule applied | clean training at every width and a ratio to GeoTransolver that does not widen (@sec-using-lr) |
| What is the covariance residual of a trained checkpoint on the GPU bfloat16 path? | rotate the inputs of a trained checkpoint under the recipe's own autocast | reported as measured; it is the number "exact" means in deployment |
| Does the architecture work on a problem that is not external aerodynamics? | a steady-conduction or Laplace acceptance case with $K = 0$ global vectors and a diffusivity as the global scalar | the contract tests pass and the error is at the level of the same-size baseline on that problem |
| Does either architecture extrapolate across geometry classes? | a split across classes rather than along one parameter of one family | none of this book's datasets provides one |
| Can the far-wake eddy-viscosity gap be closed by a principled configuration? | a configuration that does not read the discretization, at the reference width | GeoTransolver-volume ÷ ISLA at or above 0.91 without moving pressure or velocity by more than 5% |

## Engineering directions {#sec-future}

| direction | what is in place | what remains |
|---|---|---|
| Problems outside external aerodynamics | the interface accepts zero or more global vector inputs and zero or more global scalar inputs, and per-cell boundary data through the boundary-scalar channel (@sec-mt2-inputs); the contract tests cover zero and two global directions | no non-aerodynamic dataset has been trained; a conduction acceptance case is the open item, and nothing in this book's measurements depends on it |
| Cost at scale | parity with GeoTransolver's step at 10,000 tokens in half the memory on the compiled path; the exact fused geometry kernel, the default on CUDA, brings 40,000 tokens to parity and 200,000 cells to a third of GeoTransolver's training step and memory (@sec-mt2-cost, @sec-nb-isocost-prereg) | the fused kernel is single-routing only; the gap below GeoTransolver's footprint is headroom for more tokens or a wider model |
| The in-distribution price of the measure weights | its mechanism is estimator variance in the slice states, removable by more cells or by the stratified inference draw (@sec-using-sampler) | a variance-reduced consistent quadrature at a fixed cell budget beyond stratification; the weights themselves are not the target (@sec-principle) |
| Sampling conventions | the measure-weighted ISLA arms are the only ones whose convention-swap penalty converges under refinement; the baselines' does not (@sec-consistency-bench) | at 10,000 cells no architecture is consistent across conventions; the fine-mesh limit is within a few percent of reached at 40,000 |
| Query-count consistency of the interior decode | count augmentation reduces the dependence by about 40% at a small cost | a query-mass convention that does not scale with the count: the total query mass a learned fraction of the total source measure, divided by the query count, so that neither refining the source nor changing the request size moves the balance between surface and queries (the defect it removes is stated in @sec-mt2-contracts); not yet trained |

## What would change the recommendation {#sec-review-roads}

**On surface pressure at the reference size, GeoTransolver or Transolver is
the more accurate choice wherever the deployment mesher matches the
training mesher and the pose is known; ISLA is the choice wherever the
sampling may differ from the training sampling, where geometries arrive in
arbitrary poses, on the interior at matched parameters, or where memory at
scale binds.** The recommendation splits on consistency, and consistency is
a property of the frame, not of the architecture: every configuration that
centers its coordinates on a statistic of the sampled points collapses
under a sampling-density bias when the frame is taken from the biased
sample, the baselines included, and only frames that do not read
the sample hold, the relative frame among them and the ablations
of the baselines given a Horvitz–Thompson center (@sec-scoreboard-consistency).
Those ablations locate the property; GeoTransolver and
Transolver are stable, in use and published, and are not modified, so
measure weighting and a sample-free frame reach users through ISLA
(@sec-nb-ruling-released-baselines). Two outcomes would change the
recommendation.

**ISLA regains an in-distribution accuracy claim** if a principled
configuration closes the form gap on the full DrivAerML training set: the
multi-head routing run of @sec-open-questions, whose bar is written in the
anatomy's units, is the one such candidate in progress. If it closes, the
scoreboard gains a row in which the baselines no longer lead at
the reference size, and the recommendation on matched-mesher, known-pose
surface prediction becomes a trade of a few percent of accuracy against
the contracts rather than a preference for the baselines.

**The interior recommendation becomes unconditional for ISLA** only if a
principled configuration closes the far-wake eddy-viscosity gap at the
reference width without moving pressure or velocity. The single-car test
identifies the gap as capacity, the far wake beyond 0.4 body lengths
carries the whole of it, and anchor geometry, training-time sampling and
query-side inputs do not close it (@sec-interior-open); at matched
parameters the recommendation is already ISLA on pressure and velocity and
GeoTransolver-volume on eddy viscosity.

If neither fires, the recommendation stands as written, with the bounds of
this chapter attached: the program's ISLA-specific claims are exact
covariance and its lead in arbitrary poses, consistency under sampling as a
property of the relative frame, the passive query-independent decode at
its measured price, the interior velocity lead, and the cost figures of
@sec-mt2-cost, and no surface-accuracy claim in a known frame.
